newsitem.title: USA: Bill calls for U.S. withdrawal from Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Bill calls for U.S. withdrawal from Bosnia.

text.p: A bill calling for withdrawal of all U.S. ground troops from Bosnia by the end of 1997 was introduced by the chairman of the House of Representatives National Security Committee on Thursday.

The United States has about 8,000 troops in Bosnia as part of a NATO-led peacekeeping force of 31,000. Defence Secretary William Cohen has said that all U.S. troops will be out of Bosnia by the end of June 1998.
But Representative Floyd Spence said the troops should be withdrawn at least six months sooner because achieving a sustainable peace in Bosnia was unlikely under any realistic time frame.

"Under these circumstances, the U.S. should begin to work immediately toward a policy that permits the orderly withdrawal of U.S. ground forces from the theatre while continuing to provide logistics, intelligence and related support for any follow-on operation," Spence, a South Carolina Republican, said in a statement.

"It is my hope that this legislation will serve as a catalyst for a long overdue congressional debate over Bosnia policy and will help us, along with the administration, to arrive at a decision that ensures that U.S. ground forces are safely withdrawn in a timely manner," he said.

Army Gen. George Joulwan, commander of U.S. and NATO forces in Europe, warned Congress on Tuesday that the fighting readiness of his troops would suffer if he did not get an additional $2 billion to pay for peacekeeping duty in Bosnia.
The Pentagon has asked Congress to approve the special appropriation as part of the expected cost of $6.5 billion to maintain the Bosnia force.
